**Answer: the University of Bonn.**

- Aschoff studied medicine at the University of Bonn. The Nature obituary (Daan & Gwinner, 1998) says so, and English Wikipedia agrees. Both say he chose medicine after school, and Wikipedia quotes him as "lacking a specific interest."
  - https://www.nature.com/articles/24750
  - https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J%C3%BCrgen_Aschoff
- He then moved to the University of Göttingen, where his scientific career began under the physiologist Hermann Rein. This is a later step, not where he studied medicine.
  - https://www.nature.com/articles/24750
- Wikidata also lists Heidelberg University and the University of Freiburg as "educated at." Those two entries are marked as inferred from categories or a heuristic. Nothing I read says he studied medicine at either.
  - https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q75270

**Caveats:**
- I couldn't load the Auk memorial, which a search snippet said mentions several universities, so I didn't check it.
- The Wikipedia and Nature pieces are the only sources I read that state the Bonn claim directly. The Nature obituary is an independent, authoritative source.

Sources:
- [Jürgen Aschoff (1913-98), Nature](https://www.nature.com/articles/24750)
- [Jürgen Aschoff, Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J%C3%BCrgen_Aschoff)
- [Jürgen Aschoff, Wikidata](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q75270)
